subject: Linguistics
title: The Cyrillic Alphabet
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Cyrillic Alphabet.

hook.text: Russian 'Р' is pronounced 'R,' and 'Н' is 'N.' Cyrillic looks familiar—but sounds completely different.

buildup.text: Saints Cyril and Methodius created the precursor to Cyrillic in the 9th century to translate the Bible.

discovery.text: Cyrillic was based on Greek with added letters for Slavic sounds like 'sh,' 'ch,' and 'zh.'

twist.text: The Soviets adapted Cyrillic for dozens of Central Asian languages, replacing Arabic and Latin scripts.

climax.text: Today, Cyrillic is used for Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Mongolian, and many others.

punchline.text: A script built for one language now serves dozens.

quiz.question: What was Cyrillic originally created for?
options: Translating the Bible into Slavic languages
